newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain approves troops for Zaire, warns of risks.
newsitem.headline: Spain approves troops for Zaire, warns of risks.

text.p: Spain on Friday approved the dispatch of its troops as part of a U.N. multinational force to help refugees in eastern Zaire, but a government spokesman said it would be a difficult and risky operation.
Government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez said Spain's contribution would comprise 300 men and women, including medical teams, to be sent within the next two weeks.
"It will be an operation with risks but (it) is necessary," Rodriguez told journalists after Spain's Cabinet approved the contribution of its soldiers.
"The exact risk of an operation in which troops will be trying to aid people who for a long time have not received any help is unknown," he added. "There will (also) be logistical difficulties."
Spain's Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said earlier in the week it would take just two days for Spanish forces to reach Africa once a decision had been taken.

The U.N. Security Council agreed on Friday on a resolution to deploy the Candian-led multinational force to provide relief to more than one million refugees. Canada said the mission would continue despite a mass return of Rwandan refugees from Zaire.

At least 10,000 foreign troops are eventually expected in the region. The initial force will include soldiers from the United States, Canada, Britain, France, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, South Africa and Senegal.
